title: Low Water Pressure
shortDescription: Vaillant ecoTEC pressure has dropped below 0.5 bar.
fullDescription:
F.22 is the most common Vaillant ecoTEC fault. The unit has detected pressure below the operating threshold and shut down to protect the heat exchanger.

On ecoTEC plus and pro, top up via the integrated filling key (or external loop) until 1.0-1.5 bar cold and the F.22 will clear after a power cycle. Repeated F.22 indicates a leak or a waterlogged expansion vessel.
safetyWarning: Do not exceed 2 bar — the PRV will open.

causes.cause: Slow leak in radiators or piping
Filling key left in but valves closed

fixSteps.title: Top up via filling key
fixSteps.instruction: Insert the white filling key, open both valves until 1.2 bar, close, remove.

fixSteps.title: Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Press the reset button to clear F.22.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Check radiator vents, valves, and the PRV outlet outside.

whenToCallPro: Hidden leak or expansion vessel work.

faq.a: Once a year is normal; weekly means a leak.

title: Flame Detected With Gas Off
shortDescription: Phantom flame signal — possible stuck gas valve.
fullDescription:
F.27 means the ecoTEC control sees ionization (flame) when no flame should be present. Common causes: damp ignition electrode causing leakage, damaged ionization probe insulator, or a sticking gas valve.

F.27 is a safety lockout that should not be repeatedly reset.
safetyWarning: Possible stuck gas valve — call a Gas Safe engineer.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Off at the spur for 2 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Schedule service
fixSteps.instruction: Have a Gas Safe engineer inspect.

whenToCallPro: Always — stuck gas valve must be diagnosed by Gas Safe.

faq.a: Damp can cause leakage paths on the ignition assembly.

title: Ignition Failure At Start
shortDescription: Burner failed to ignite after retries.
fullDescription:
F.28 is the Vaillant ecoTEC ignition lockout. After three failed ignition attempts the boiler hard locks until reset.

Most common UK cause is gas supply issues (closed meter valve, low LP, air in line after meter swap). Other causes: fouled ignition rod, plugged condensate trap, failed gas valve.
safetyWarning: If you smell gas, evacuate and call 0800 111 999.

causes.cause: Closed gas valve at meter or boiler

fixSteps.title: Verify gas
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm another gas appliance lights normally.

fixSteps.title: Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Press Reset and observe ignition.

whenToCallPro: Gas Safe engineer for pressure verification.

faq.a: Yes — air in the line; the engineer should re-bleed.

title: Flame Loss During Run
shortDescription: Established flame extinguished mid-cycle.
fullDescription: F.29 is logged when the ecoTEC ignites successfully but loses flame during operation. Look for low gas pressure under load, oxidized ionization rod, or condensate flooding the burner.
safetyWarning: Repeated F.29 means an underlying fault — do not just keep resetting.

fixSteps.title: Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Press Reset and observe.

fixSteps.title: Service
fixSteps.instruction: Have an engineer clean ionization rod and check gas pressure.

whenToCallPro: Combustion analyzer check.

faq.a: Gas pressure droop on shared meters.

title: Gas Pressure Fault
shortDescription: Gas inlet pressure below required minimum.
fullDescription:
F.54 is logged when the ecoTEC's gas pressure switch reports low inlet pressure. The boiler refuses to start to avoid incomplete combustion.

Common causes are an undersized gas pipe to the boiler, supplier outage, or a closed meter valve.
safetyWarning: Gas Safe required for any gas-pressure work.

fixSteps.title: Verify gas
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm meter valve open and other appliances work.

whenToCallPro: Gas Safe engineer.

faq.a: Yes — common after upstream supply work.

title: Pump / Pressure Sensor Fault
shortDescription: No pressure rise when pump starts.
fullDescription:
F.75 is one of the most common Vaillant fault codes. The boiler expects to see a small pressure rise when the pump starts; if it does not, F.75 is logged.

Causes include a failed/seized pump, waterlogged expansion vessel, faulty pressure sensor, or air in the boiler.
safetyWarning: Do not bypass — the pump test is a flow safety check.

fixSteps.title: Bleed
fixSteps.instruction: Bleed radiators and the boiler at the pump bleed screw.

fixSteps.title: Free pump
fixSteps.instruction: Free the pump shaft via the central slotted screw.

whenToCallPro: Pump replacement or expansion vessel work.

faq.a: Standing pumps seize after summer; recharge expansion vessel annually.

title: Flow Temperature Sensor Interruption
shortDescription: The flow (NTC) temperature sensor circuit is open.
fullDescription:
Fault code F.00 on Vaillant ecoTEC boilers indicates an open circuit in the central heating flow temperature sensor (NTC). The boiler cannot read the supply water temperature and will lock out for safety.

Usually caused by a disconnected sensor connector, a damaged sensor, or wiring break.
safetyWarning: This error involves a gas-fired appliance. If you smell gas at any time, do not operate switches or attempt repairs. Evacuate, leave doors open, and call your gas utility from a safe location. Repairs to gas valves, burners, or flue components must be performed by a licensed gas engineer or technician.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Sensor Plug
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; remove the front cover and reseat the flow NTC connector at the sensor and PCB.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Engineer measures NTC resistance against the Vaillant table; replace if open.

whenToCallPro: If reseating the connector does not clear the fault, a Gas Safe engineer should test and replace the sensor.

faq.q: What's the difference between F.00 and F.01?
faq.a: F.00 is the flow sensor (open circuit on heating flow), F.01 is the return sensor.

title: Return Temperature Sensor Interruption
shortDescription: The return (NTC) temperature sensor circuit is open.
fullDescription:
Fault code F.01 indicates the Vaillant ecoTEC boiler has detected an open circuit on the central heating return NTC sensor. The unit cannot calculate temperature differential across the heat exchanger and locks out.

Causes mirror F.00: connector issues, broken wiring, or a failed thermistor.
safetyWarning: This error involves a gas-fired appliance. If you smell gas at any time, do not operate switches or attempt repairs. Evacuate, leave doors open, and call your gas utility from a safe location. Repairs to gas valves, burners, or flue components must be performed by a licensed gas engineer or technician.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Connector
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; reseat return NTC sensor plug.

fixSteps.title: Test/Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Engineer measures resistance and replaces if open.

whenToCallPro: If the connector is fine, a Gas Safe engineer must test and replace the sensor.

faq.a: It locks the boiler out as a safety measure to prevent overheating; not immediately dangerous, but service is needed.

title: Flow Sensor Short Circuit
shortDescription: The flow temperature sensor circuit is shorted.
fullDescription:
Fault F.10 indicates a short circuit on the central heating flow NTC sensor wiring. The PCB sees zero or near-zero resistance and locks out the boiler.

Common causes include a pinched wire grounding to the chassis, a failed sensor that has shorted, or moisture in a connector.
safetyWarning: This error involves a gas-fired appliance. If you smell gas at any time, do not operate switches or attempt repairs. Evacuate, leave doors open, and call your gas utility from a safe location. Repairs to gas valves, burners, or flue components must be performed by a licensed gas engineer or technician.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; inspect flow NTC harness for chafing or grounding.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Engineer replaces the NTC and confirms resistance to spec.

whenToCallPro: Have a Gas Safe engineer test and replace the sensor or repair the wiring.

faq.q: Why does F.10 happen after pump replacement?
faq.a: Sensor wires are sometimes pinched during reassembly. Inspect the harness routing carefully.

title: EEPROM Error
shortDescription: Internal PCB EEPROM read/write error.
fullDescription:
Fault F.63 indicates an internal memory (EEPROM) error on the Vaillant PCB. The board cannot reliably read its calibration data and locks out.

This is usually a hardware issue requiring PCB replacement, sometimes following a power surge.
safetyWarning: This error involves a gas-fired appliance. If you smell gas at any time, do not operate switches or attempt repairs. Evacuate, leave doors open, and call your gas utility from a safe location. Repairs to gas valves, burners, or flue components must be performed by a licensed gas engineer or technician.

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect mains for 60 seconds and restore. If F.63 returns, the PCB is failing.

fixSteps.title: Replace PCB
fixSteps.instruction: Engineer replaces and configures the PCB to match boiler model and gas type.

whenToCallPro: F.63 almost always requires PCB replacement by a Gas Safe engineer.

faq.q: Could a surge protector prevent this?
faq.a: Yes, a quality whole-home or boiler-dedicated surge protector reduces the risk of EEPROM corruption.

title: PCB / Sensor Electronic Fault
shortDescription: PCB has detected internal sensor short to its electronics.
fullDescription:
Fault F.64 indicates the Vaillant PCB has detected a short circuit between flow/return NTC inputs, often caused by a damaged sensor harness shorting two sensor channels together, or by an internal PCB defect.

It is often confused with F.00/F.01, but the difference is the inputs are shorted to each other rather than open.
safetyWarning: This error involves a gas-fired appliance. If you smell gas at any time, do not operate switches or attempt repairs. Evacuate, leave doors open, and call your gas utility from a safe location. Repairs to gas valves, burners, or flue components must be performed by a licensed gas engineer or technician.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Sensor Harness
fixSteps.instruction: Engineer disconnects sensors and measures harness for shorts.

fixSteps.title: Replace Harness or PCB
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the sensor harness or PCB depending on test results.

whenToCallPro: Diagnosis requires a Gas Safe engineer with multimeter access to the sensor harness.

faq.a: PCB-related faults are typically covered within Vaillant's parts warranty period.

title: PCB Temperature Too High
shortDescription: The PCB temperature sensor is reporting an excessive board temperature.
fullDescription:
Fault F.65 indicates the Vaillant ecoTEC PCB has overheated. This usually means the boiler is in a poorly ventilated cupboard, the boiler casing is loose, or the PCB cooling path is blocked.

Less commonly, the PCB temperature sensor itself has failed.
safetyWarning: This error involves a gas-fired appliance. If you smell gas at any time, do not operate switches or attempt repairs. Evacuate, leave doors open, and call your gas utility from a safe location. Repairs to gas valves, burners, or flue components must be performed by a licensed gas engineer or technician.

fixSteps.title: Improve Ventilation
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure boiler clearances meet manufacturer minimums; remove blockages above and below.

fixSteps.title: Check Casing
fixSteps.instruction: Engineer verifies casing is sealed and PCB enclosure is correctly fitted.

whenToCallPro: If improving ventilation does not solve the issue, an engineer should test and potentially replace the PCB.

faq.a: Improving cabinet airflow with passive vents is preferred; ducted fans are rarely required.

title: Flame Signal Implausible
shortDescription: The PCB sees an invalid flame signal condition.
fullDescription:
Fault F.67 indicates the flame ionisation signal received by the PCB is implausible (e.g., flame seen with no gas valve open). It is a safety lockout to prevent unsafe operation.

Common causes include a damaged flame rectification probe, a wet PCB, or a failed PCB.
safetyWarning: This error involves a gas-fired appliance. If you smell gas at any time, do not operate switches or attempt repairs. Evacuate, leave doors open, and call your gas utility from a safe location. Repairs to gas valves, burners, or flue components must be performed by a licensed gas engineer or technician.

fixSteps.title: Engineer Inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Engineer inspects flame probe, ceramic, and lead for damage.

fixSteps.title: Replace Probe / PCB
fixSteps.instruction: Replace flame probe and PCB if water-damaged.

whenToCallPro: All flame circuit faults must be handled by a Gas Safe engineer.

faq.q: Why after a leak above the boiler?
faq.a: Water reaching the PCB or flame lead is a common trigger; thoroughly dry and replace components as needed.

title: Flame Signal Unstable
shortDescription: The flame ionisation signal is fluctuating outside the allowed band.
fullDescription:
Fault F.68 on Vaillant ecoTEC boilers indicates the flame signal is unstable during firing. This may be caused by a dirty flame rectification probe, incorrect gas/air ratio, recirculation of flue gases, or an incorrectly set CO2 ratio after an APS / venturi service.

It commonly appears after part replacements, gas works, or vent modifications.
safetyWarning: This error involves a gas-fired appliance. If you smell gas at any time, do not operate switches or attempt repairs. Evacuate, leave doors open, and call your gas utility from a safe location. Repairs to gas valves, burners, or flue components must be performed by a licensed gas engineer or technician.
symptoms: Boiler cuts out shortly after firing
Yellow flame visible at sight glass

fixSteps.title: Engineer Service
fixSteps.instruction: Engineer cleans flame probe and verifies CO2 setting with a calibrated combustion analyzer.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Flue
fixSteps.instruction: Verify flue assembly is sealed and no recirculation between intake and exhaust occurs.

whenToCallPro: F.68 must be diagnosed by a Gas Safe engineer with a calibrated flue gas analyzer.

faq.q: Will cleaning the burner clear F.68?
faq.a: Sometimes; but combustion settings must always be verified after any burner-side work.

title: Invalid Device Specific Number / Display PCB Mismatch
shortDescription: The display module and main PCB have incompatible product codes after a parts replacement.
fullDescription:
Fault F.70 on Vaillant ecoTEC boilers indicates an invalid combination of display and main PCB device-specific numbers (DSN). It almost always appears immediately after a board or display replacement when the technician has not programmed the correct DSN code into the new component.

Until the DSN is set per the Vaillant service manual, the boiler will not operate.
safetyWarning: This error involves a gas-fired appliance. If you smell gas at any time, do not operate switches or attempt repairs. Evacuate, leave doors open, and call your gas utility from a safe location. Repairs to gas valves, burners, or flue components must be performed by a licensed gas engineer or technician.

causes.cause: DSN code not programmed after PCB swap

fixSteps.title: Program DSN
fixSteps.instruction: A Vaillant-trained engineer enters the correct DSN code from the boiler data plate into D.093 (or model-equivalent diagnostic).

fixSteps.title: Verify Operation
fixSteps.instruction: Power cycle and verify the boiler reports the correct model identity and runs through ignition.

whenToCallPro: DSN programming is engineer-only; do not attempt without the boiler service manual and data plate.

faq.q: Where do I find the DSN?
faq.a: On the silver data plate inside the casing of your specific boiler model.

title: Flow/Return Temperature Sensor Difference
shortDescription: The flow and return NTC sensors disagree by more than the allowed tolerance.
fullDescription:
Fault F.72 on Vaillant ecoTEC boilers indicates the heating flow and return NTC sensors are reporting temperatures that differ by more than the allowed amount under static or running conditions. It is most often caused by a sensor that has drifted or by one sensor not being properly seated against its pocket.

Replacement is usually done as a flow + return NTC pair.
safetyWarning: This error involves a gas-fired appliance. If you smell gas at any time, do not operate switches or attempt repairs. Evacuate, leave doors open, and call your gas utility from a safe location. Repairs to gas valves, burners, or flue components must be performed by a licensed gas engineer or technician.
symptoms: Boiler locks out shortly after firing

fixSteps.title: Bleed System
fixSteps.instruction: Bleed radiators and verify pressure 1.0-1.5 bar cold to rule out air.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Sensors
fixSteps.instruction: Engineer power-cycles, removes and reseats both NTCs in their pockets.

fixSteps.title: Replace NTC Pair
fixSteps.instruction: Replace both NTCs as a pair if one tests out of spec.

whenToCallPro: If bleeding and reseating do not resolve F.72, have a Gas Safe engineer test and replace the NTC pair.

faq.a: They drift at similar rates; replacing as a pair avoids recurrence within months.
